overview: The cell's energy currency in its 'charged' and 'spent' forms, differing by just one phosphate group.
genZNote: ATP: fully charged battery. ADP: the same battery after it's given up a charge.

aspects.label: Energy State
aspects.valueA: High-energy molecule; releases energy when the terminal phosphate bond is hydrolysed.
aspects.valueB: Lower-energy molecule; can be 're-charged' back into ATP by adding a phosphate.

aspects.label: Role
aspects.valueA: The immediate energy source used to power cellular work.
aspects.valueB: Formed after ATP releases energy; gets recycled back into ATP during respiration.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: ATP to ADP conversion releases about 7.3 kcal/mol of energy under standard conditions — a frequently quoted figure.
overlay.memoryTrick: ATP = Adenosine TriPhosphate (three). ADP = Adenosine DiPhosphate (two, one 'spent').
overlay.commonMisconception: ATP is not 'stored' in large amounts in cells — it's constantly made and used up within seconds, recycled thousands of times a day.
